answer: An agent market weights each bidder's access to paid tasks by collateral locked for 30 days, rather than by account count. Whether a task tracks a sparrow, maps a dune, or classifies a nebula, splitting 100 tokens across 100 identities gives the same total bidding weight as staking them in one account. To gain more influence, an attacker must lock more capital and bear its opportunity cost for the full period; creating aliases adds no weight.
